Drugs Controller General of India (DCGI) Rajeev Raghuvan- shi has asked state and Union Territory (UT)-level drug con- trol bodies to direct all manu- facturers, vendors and suppliers of high-risk pharma- ceutical-grade solvents to reg- ister on the Centre’s DMS immediately, according to a document seen by Business Standard. “It shall be ensured that no batch of pharmaceutical grade of these solvents should be dis- tributed without uploading the required details sought on the DMS and obtaining system gen- erated no-objection certiﬁcate (NOC),” a CDSCO order dated October 27 states. The order includes 10 such excipients, including propy- lene glycol, glycerine, maltitol and sorbitol. These ingredients are used in liquid medicines and cough syrups, and regula- tors treat them as high-risk for contamination. Officials in the know told Business Standard that states have been requested to accord high priority to this matter and ensure strict compliance across all manufacturing and supply units. While backing the move, industry executives said that improper implementation could lead to possible clearance delays as licensing and approval requests might come in bulk. “While the notiﬁcation pri- marily applies to solvent manu- facturers and suppliers rather than formulation manufac- turers, its implementation could lead to temporary supply disruptions as manufacturers complete registration and align with the new reporting require- ments,” said Saurabh Agarwal, director and chief executive officer at Mumbai-based HAB Pharmaceuticals and Research. These are likely to be short- term challenges. “In the longer run, this initiative will help strengthen traceability, improve regulatory oversight and build greater conﬁdence in the pharma supply chain,” he added.
